A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NaviMaster. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or redrawn in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original GUI, spatial-affordance, and ObjectNav evaluations, ablation results, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, expanded ablations, a visual-relation benchmark, and case studies in Section 4 and Appendices G–H.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix C change the stated GUI scrolling interface from start/end coordinates to four directional choices. The trajectory pipeline, history conditioning, GRPO, and reward design remain stable. Appendix B still specifies coordinate-based scrolling, so implementation consistency is unresolved.

E1.justification: v2 extends mobile GUI evaluation to GUIAct-Web, OmniAct-Web, and OmniAct-Desktop, and adds in-domain Odyssey evaluation. It also introduces relational UI instructions requiring spatial inference and a combined browser-search/embodied-navigation case study. The original training sources and embodied benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: The GUI comparison adds UI-AGILE and removes v1's separate OS-Atlas-PRO row; OS-Atlas-7B remains with broader reported coverage. Spatial-affordance comparators are unchanged. OmniActor is discussed but explicitly excluded from evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix D change reported training from 7,000 samples over ten epochs to 20,000 over three epochs. v2 adds grounding accuracy as a primary GUI metric, a 4,800-case Odyssey evaluation, and a 100-instance relational test. Ablations also introduce specialist-model averages and revised benchmark selections and parameter sweeps.

E4.justification: v2 adds mixing-ratio sensitivity, 7k-versus-20k data-scale comparisons, three reward-weight variants, a visual-reasoning comparison, and a combined-domain case study. Existing base-model, reward, training-order, and embodied-data-source analyses persist with revised results and presentation; the latter two move to Appendix G.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's Table 7, titled Detailed statistics, supplies point results rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark and ablation results and revises many existing scores. NaviMaster's AC-High SR changes from 54.0 to 55.89, while RefSpatial changes from 23.32 to 19.49 under the revised training budget; these are not controlled version-to-version gains. ObjectNav table values remain unchanged. Baseline Type scores disappear, while NaviMaster Type results continue in Appendix E.

T1.justification: Appendix C, Equation 12, revises the formal GUI action set by replacing coordinate-to-coordinate scrolling with discrete directions. The MDP statement, projection equations, GRPO advantage, and reward equations otherwise remain unchanged. The added discussion of learning across MDPs introduces no theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central unified-agent, trajectory-collection, dense-reward, and OOD-generalization claims remain. The introduction and Figure 1 add an explicit visual-reasoning advantage, claiming that joint training develops transferable structural representations beyond task-specific correlations.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting mixed training to reduced single-MDP overfitting and transferable spatial reasoning. It interprets new analyses as supporting balanced mixtures and the selected reward weights. The existing limitations, including the absence of training trajectories interleaving both domains, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 updates the documented training sample and epoch counts, specifies the Odyssey evaluation sample count, details additional ablation configurations, and adds a project-homepage link. The original prompts, hardware description, and most hyperparameters are retained; the PDFs do not establish additional code or data availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to OmniAct, UI-AGILE, and OmniActor. It acknowledges OmniActor as concurrent work unifying 2D and 3D tasks and explains its exclusion from comparisons. The broader related-work discussion and positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the abstract and main narrative, expands the action-space explanation, and shortens the conclusion. Section 4.4 is reorganized as Discussions and Analysis, with existing analyses moved into the new Appendix G and case studies relabeled Appendix H. The overall document structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The GUI table is redesigned with platform groups and GR/SR columns, while Type reporting receives a separate appendix table. Figures 2 and 4–6 are substantially redrawn or reorganized, and Table 7 and Figure 10 are added. Existing case-study Figures 7–9 are retained.

improvement.justification: Broader GUI evaluation and new mixing-ratio, data-scale, and reward-weight controls strengthen evidence for generalization and design choices. Benefits are tempered by new inconsistencies: Figure 4a reports 40.6 average SR for the 3B model, whereas the corresponding Table 7 values average approximately 34.02, and the scrolling definition conflicts with the retained prompt. The expanded validation provides a limited net improvement.
